overview.text: The Murom icon is associated with Prince Constantine’s Christian mission and with Saint Basil of Ryazan. The published history connects Murom and Ryazan while distinguishing later copies and commemorations.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of the named copyrighted publication; full-text reproduction permission has not been established. Traditional events and published interpretations remain attributed.

blocks.text: This seventeenth-century example is identified in its file record as the Murom Mother of God. It shows the Child reclining across Mary’s arms and reaching toward her face. It is a historical depiction of the named type, rather than proof that the earliest revered object survives in this file.

blocks.text: The OCA describes Constantine bringing the image from Kiev and a hostile crowd changing its response when he approaches with the icon. A later story follows Basil carrying it on a journey over water. Miraculous events remain attributed to the church account. The icon thereafter becomes associated with Ryazan as well as Murom.
